text:
jordan_support: customer on Dedicated experiencing intermittent 502/504s only when requests go through corporate proxy chain. They say it started after a proxy upgrade. Repro steps pasted below — can we triage?

marta_netops: can you share the curl/tcpdump output and which host exactly (FQDN/IP)? is it just redwood-api or other endpoints too?

devon_onprem: only redwood-api.example.com (customer is using a CNAME to our gateway). other tls sites fine. quick curl from bastion: 
```
$ curl -v https://redwood-api.example.com/v1/generate 
*   Trying 198.51.100.22...
* Connected to corp-proxy.local (10.10.10.1) port 3128 (#0)
* Establish HTTP proxy tunnel to redwood-api.example.com:443
> CONNECT redwood-api.example.com:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: redwood-api.example.com
> Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* Proxy replied OK to CONNECT request
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* SSL_read: errno=104, Connection reset by peer
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) OpenSSL SSL_read: Connection was reset, errno 104
```

jordan_support: stack trace from our side shows the connection gets reset during server_hello -> we return 502 because stream closed. customer says proxy logs show repeated CONNECTs and occasional 502 responses from the proxy.

sam_engineer: possible causes: proxy performing TLS inspection (intercepts/SNI rewrite), proxy chain timeouts, or egress firewall kicking in on specific IP ranges. also some proxies rewrite SNI or drop connections when SNI doesn't match allowlist.

marta_netops: on our side we've seen this when a middle proxy requires the CONNECT host to be an IP rather than hostname when doing SNI passthrough, or when a transparent TLS-inspecting box does imperfect ssl_bump handling. do we have packet capture from the boundary?

devon_onprem: customer can run tcpdump but they're air-gapped so they requested guidance. suggested capture command: 
```
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/redwood_probe.pcap host 198.51.100.22 and port 443
# or filter by proxy IP:
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/proxy_probe.pcap host 10.10.10.1 and port 3128
```

jordan_support: also ask them to get proxy logs for the CONNECT sequence. key things to look for: repeated CONNECTs, 200 then immediate reset, any log lines about "TLS handshake failed", "sni rewrite" or "policy deny on server_name".

sam_engineer: workaround we suggested that often works: 1) add redwood-api FQDN/IPs to egress allowlist so proxy does TLS passthrough (no interception), 2) ensure CONNECT method is allowed end-to-end and not rewritten, 3) if using an explicit proxy chain, ensure the intermediate proxy forwards the original CONNECT without setting a new SNI header.

marta_netops: specific Squid notes: if they upgraded to a version with aggressive ssl_bump rules, set acl to allow TLS passthrough for redwood-api.example.com and configure ssl_bump none for that acl. if using an enterprise TLS forward proxy (Bluecoat/FS), check the SSL inspection policy for exceptions.

devon_onprem: i'll ask customer for: tcpdump pcap, proxy CONNECT logs (timestamps matching 2201112222..2201112622 window), and their corporate firewall egress rules. they also mentioned CDN in front of redwood — CNAME -> cdn.example.net -> our edge. could be CDN IPs blocked.

jordan_support: good catch — ask them to whitelist both the API FQDN and the edge IP ranges (we provided ranges in our onboarding doc). if they can't whitelist IPs, they must allow TLS passthrough for the FQDN.

infra-bot: automated note: please include agent_region, client_time, and the SDK request-id from the failing request to help correlate on our side.

sam_engineer: final checklist for customer to send back: 1) curl -v output (as above), 2) tcpdump pcap, 3) proxy logs around the timestamps, 4) firewall egress ACLs, 5) whether any TLS inspection appliance was rolled out in the last week. once we have those we can confirm if it's SNI rewrite / MITM or a connection drop in the chain.

marta_netops: for short term mitigation, they can route Dedicated traffic via a site-to-site VPN to bypass corp proxies (if available) or use a permitted egress bastion that has direct internet.

jordan_support: thanks — i've opened a ticket and asked the customer to provide the artifacts. assigning to @marta_netops and @sam_engineer to follow up. :eyes:
